scope.goal: Store, query and replace the weekly operating days of each fulfillment node while preserving all existing allocation behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: FulfillmentNode owns a non-null, non-empty immutable set of weekly working days.
New fulfillment nodes default to all seven DayOfWeek values without changing the existing create API.
Existing fulfillment nodes are backfilled with all seven days by Flyway.
GET /api/v1/fulfillment-nodes/{id}/working-days returns the configured days in deterministic Monday-to-Sunday order.
PUT /api/v1/fulfillment-nodes/{id}/working-days replaces the complete set and is idempotent.
Missing, null, empty or invalid working-day payloads return a structured 400 response.
Invalid fulfillment node IDs return structured 400 responses and missing nodes return structured 404 responses.
Persistence uses fulfillment_node_working_days with a composite primary key and foreign key; no CSV or JSON collection storage is used.
Orders, capacity-aware allocation and existing Fulfillment Node endpoints preserve their behavior.
./gradlew clean test --no-daemon passes and manual Postman-compatible cURLs are documented.
outOfScope: Rejecting allocation based on the current day.
Holidays, exceptional closures or date-specific calendars.
Working hours, cutoff times or time zones per fulfillment node.
Automatic node selection, fallback or rescheduling.
Changes to Orders domain or Orders API.
Events, transactional outbox, Kafka, idempotency and observability.
A generic BusinessCalendar aggregate or scheduling engine.
constraints: Keep the domain free from Spring, JPA and HTTP concerns.
Use a normalized relational table and Flyway migration.
Do not modify Orders production code.
Do not enforce working days during allocation in this task.
Do not commit, push, create a PR or merge.
